claim: van Rijn and Hutter (KDD 2018) extend fANOVA hyperparameter importance from a single dataset to meta-learning across many OpenML datasets, analyzing SVM, random forest, and Adaboost separately (not jointly).
quoted_support: We apply this methodology using the experimental meta-data available on OpenML to determine the most important hyperparameters of support vector machines, random forests and Adaboost, and to infer priors for all their hyperparameters.

claim: This paper never crosses model/algorithm class against optimizer/search-strategy class as two jointly-varied factors, and does not even include model-class choice as a decomposed hyperparameter (unlike Hutter14's Auto-WEKA experiment).
scope_conditions: Whole paper -- SVM, RF, Adaboost analyzed as separate, independent fANOVA runs
quoted_support: Given an algorithm, what are generally its most important hyperparameters, and what are typically good values for these?

claim: The only mentions of 'optimizer' in this paper refer to a fixed downstream HPO search method consuming the fANOVA-derived priors, run with 10 random seeds -- not a second factor being variance-decomposed against algorithm class.
quoted_support: Each optimizer was ran with 10 different random [seeds].
